notes: Second-pass counts describe the 74 first-pass sentences. The two 'textbook' sentences in section 0 had no retrieved text and were removed (classed unsupported). The cell wall sentence was supported by a PubMed abstract (7372662), not PMC2702430. Allergy-label, Northern Care Alliance, allergy-testing and 'partly treated bacteria' sentences were not retrievable and were cut. The probenecid sentence was wrong (emc says use together is not recommended, not that the amount is adjusted); interaction list otherwise matches emc SmPC product 526 (cited as /smpc; the search returned that product's SmPC under a pil-style link, check the URL resolves). 'Finish the course' is kept only as NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin advice (an ICB page; weak) because nhs.uk wording was not returned. Antimicrobial resistance sentences cite Northern Moor Medical Practice (weak GP-practice page; the search blended pages so the attribution is a best guess; consider the NHS Antibiotics page). The final text contains ONE textbook sentence, 'In the UK, 999 is the number to call in an emergency', used so the urgency names its route since the retrieved NHS text did not state 999. The NHS pregnancy page says it is 'safe' in pregnancy; the final wording avoids 'safe'. Glandular fever wording follows NHS (rash; tell a doctor first); the existing medications.json entry says amoxicillin 'should be avoided' in glandular fever and calls the rash non-allergic, which this pass did not verify. A MedlinePlus (US) result said amoxicillin may reduce hormonal contraceptive effect; the NHS (UK) statement is used and the conflict is flagged. Thrush, anaphylaxis wording and 'up to two months' came from search summaries of the NHS side-effects page. Final text is about 1,000 words in the article block.
